name: prose mentioning a trailer, no commit invoked
why: REGRESSION 2026-09-23: v1 matched any command that merely mentioned it, and blocked the commit documenting the rule

name: documenting the rule while committing it
command:
python3 - <<'PY'
# the hook blocks any git commit whose message has a Co-Authored-By: Claude line
PY
why: REGRESSION 2026-09-23: this exact shape blocked the fix for itself

name: commit whose message discusses attribution without carrying it
command:
git commit -m "feat: reject attribution trailers

The guard rejects a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer and the Generated with line. Before it existed the rule was checked by hand after every commit."
why: THE anchoring case, and it needs the verbatim shape: prose containing `Co-Authored-By: Claude` inside a real commit message. Without the ^ anchor the hook blocks every commit that documents the rule it enforces — which is what 254b969 was. The command-position cases do not cover this; they exit before the trailer check runs.
